audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] calls her poke 'W Swirlseed' and early/whys[1] talk about 'her W ring' and 'her W outer ring'. Swirlseed is her E. Her W is Watch Out! Eep!, and the ring geometry the entry is reaching for belongs to a third ability.
audit.why: Three separate abilities are being blended into one imaginary 'W ring'. Swirlseed (E) is a flat 12s, 700-range seed that damages and slows and keeps rolling if it hits nothing. Watch Out! Eep! (W) is 14/13/12/11/10 and hits an area with heavy damage in the centre. The edge bonus the entry keeps calling a 'ring' is Blooming Blows (Q), which deals extra TRUE damage on its outer edge — which is why armour is not the answer to her poke.
audit.corrected: Swirlseed is E, flat 12s at 700 range. Watch Out! Eep! is W, 14s at rank 1, heaviest in the centre. Blooming Blows (Q) is the one with the edge bonus, and that edge is true damage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (Q Blooming Blows trueDamage; W Watch Out! Eep! cd 14/13/12/11/10; E Swirlseed cd 12 range 700)

audit.whatIsWrong: Lilting Lullaby is mentioned once, as 'R sleep chains' in a throwaway late-game clause. The condition on it is never stated anywhere, and neither is Dream-Laden Bough.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it is entirely absent. Lilting Lullaby only affects enemies who already have Dream Dust on them, and Dream Dust comes from her passive, which lands whenever any of her skills hits you. So the poke is not just chip — it is ultimate setup. A Trundle who walks into a fight with a Swirlseed already ticking on him can be put to sleep; a Trundle who breaks contact first cannot be touched by her R at all. That single fact reorders how the whole lane should be played.
audit.corrected: Lilting Lullaby only drowses and sleeps enemies already carrying Dream Dust, and Dream Dust is her passive — it lands from any skill of hers that hits you. Arrive at the fight unchipped.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (P Dream-Laden Bough; R Lilting Lullaby, cd 150/130/110, range 1600)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and whys[4] both claim that draining her Magic Resist with Subjugate makes Trundle's autos hit harder — 'draining her MR mid-fight means your autos hit harder', 'drain her MR early in the all-in and your W-buffed autos become lethal'.
audit.why: Trundle's autos and Chomp are physical. Taking Magic Resist off Lillia does nothing for them. What the theft actually buys is the other half: Subjugate gives the stolen resistances to Trundle, so the MR is defensive value against her — and against Lillia, who is entirely magic damage plus the true damage on Blooming Blows' edge, that is exactly the half that matters. The advice is right to cast R early; the reason given is backwards.
audit.corrected: The MR you take off her is MR you are wearing against her own magic damage — that is the defensive half of Subjugate, not an offensive one.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R Subjugate steals Health, Armor and Magic Resistance, doubled over 4s)

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows is the tracked cooldown across the whole entry — loading says 'Engage only on Blooming Blows's cooldown', breakdown.mid says 'when it is down, run your full pattern', report[9] and dosFull[0] repeat it. Neither ultimate ever gets a number.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4. A four-to-six second cooldown is not a window — telling the player to engage on it describes something that is available on almost every trade, so the rule silently means 'engage whenever'. The cooldowns that actually gate this lane are Swirlseed at a flat 12s and Watch Out! Eep! at 14s, and above all the two ultimates: Subjugate 120/100/80 against Lilting Lullaby 150/130/110. Trundle's R is up first at every rank and the gap widens to 80s against 110s.
audit.corrected: Blooming Blows is 6s falling to 4s — it is never meaningfully down. Trade around Swirlseed's flat 12s instead, and note Subjugate 120/100/80 beats Lilting Lullaby 150/130/110 at every rank.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (Q cd 6/5.5/5/4.5/4; E cd 12; R cd 150/130/110)

audit.whatIsWrong: early credits Chomp with an 'attack speed debuff' and spikes[0] says it 'slows her attack speed'. Pillar of Ice is called 'your best early tool' with no cooldown attached.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement — there is no attack-speed component. The attack speed in this matchup is Frozen Domain's, on a separate 18/17/16/15/14. And Pillar of Ice is Trundle's longest non-ultimate cooldown at 21s at rank 1, which is precisely why 'best early tool' needs a number: spend it on her exit route, not on chip, or the next 21 seconds are spent without it.
audit.corrected: Chomp is a flat 3.5s attack reset that saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement. Pillar of Ice is 21s at rank 1 — one bad pillar costs the next trade.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Q Chomp cd 3.5 range 300; W cd 18/17/16/15/14; E cd 21/19.5/18/16.5/15)

edits.before: Level 1 you bite her on every last-hit attempt — Chomp's AD steal and attack speed debuff mean even a glancing trade chips her more than it chips you, and King's Tribute healing off minion deaths keeps you topped. The problem starts at level 2: Lillia's Blooming Blows passive gives her movement speed every time she hits you with her W ring, and her long auto range means she can poke without walking into your Frozen Domain. Place W conservatively at level 2 — use it to win the trades she DOES walk into, not to chase her into open lane where the domain expires and she outruns you. At level 3, Pillar is your best early tool: drop it behind her escape path the moment she burns Blooming Blows or walks to farm, and run the full Q-bites inside W.
edits.after: Level 1 you bite her on every last-hit attempt — Chomp is a flat 3.5s attack reset that saps her AD and briefly slows her, and King's Tribute heals you off every minion that dies near you. The problem starts at level 2: Blooming Blows stacks her movement speed off any spell of hers that lands, and Swirlseed (E) pokes from 700 range without her ever entering your Frozen Domain. Place W conservatively at level 2 — use it to win the trades she DOES walk into, not to chase her into open lane where the domain expires and she outruns you. At level 3, Pillar is your best early tool, but it is 21s at rank 1: spend it behind her escape path as she steps up to farm, then run the full Q-bites inside W.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the hardest stretch — Lillia's W and passive speed let her trade on her terms, kiting to the edge of your domain and refreshing stacks before you can land a second Chomp. Do not chase her out of the ice zone; if she refuses to fight inside it, farm and wait. Level 6 changes the math: pop Subjugate the instant she commits a full Blooming Blows rotation into you, because draining her MR mid-fight (she stacks ability haste and AP items) means your autos hit harder while your own resistances climb. The all-in is yours if Blooming Blows is on cooldown when you press R — she has no instant escape from your range once the resist-drain lands.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the hardest stretch — Blooming Blows returns in 6s at rank 1 and stacks her movement speed, so she kites to the edge of your domain and refreshes before you land a second Chomp. Do not chase her out of the ice zone; if she refuses to fight inside it, farm and wait. Level 6 changes the math, and not the way most entries say: Lilting Lullaby only puts enemies who already carry her passive Dream Dust to sleep, so every stray Swirlseed she lands on you is ultimate setup. Arrive at the fight clean. Then cast Subjugate early — 120/100/80 against her 150/130/110, and the Magic Resist you take off her is MR you wear against her own damage.

edits.before: With two items you are the undisputed side-lane threat — Lillia cannot 1v1 a Trundle who has Trinity Force and any tank item, because Subjugate strips her MR and W domain lets you match her movement speed burst in an extended chase. Force her to either answer your split or let you take structures; in team fights, Subjugate their beefiest frontliner and let your team deal with Lillia's AoE. End before the very latest stages of the game — a fed Lillia with full AP and R sleep chains can flip team fights — but your individual duel advantage means the side lane is yours all the way to nexus.
edits.after: With two items you are the undisputed side-lane threat — Lillia cannot 1v1 a Trundle who has Trinity Force and any tank item, because Subjugate takes Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds while W matches her speed burst. Force her to either answer your split or let you take structures; in team fights, Subjugate their beefiest frontliner and let your team deal with Lillia's AoE. Her R only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust, so break contact from her poke before a fight starts, not after — a chipped Trundle is a sleeping Trundle, and the side lane is yours as long as you walk in clean.

Eep! is W (14s at rank 1), and the outer-edge bonus belongs to Blooming Blows (Q) and is TRUE damage, which is why armour is not the answer to her poke.
